headline: Medium risk: shared data and broad egress create leakage and cascading-error pathways; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, agent_a uses CLI/session memory and agent_b exposes a REST API; if outputs are manually bridged or copied into the other, prompt-like content could influence behavior. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not observed.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_b are pasted into agent_a prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced, the bridge becomes direct.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering on imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while agent_b has broad network egress. Even without a documented shared filesystem, any handoff of agent_a outputs into agent_b can leak sensitive content to a third party. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded to agent_b, sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
IF both agents share a workspace or logs, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route sensitive agent_a outputs into agent_b.
Redact personal and finance data before transfer.
Restrict agent_b egress to approved endpoints only.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of support data.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on the transfer path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and session memory, but no write-capable shared resource is documented for either agent. agent_b only shows REST API access, so overlapping mutable-state writes are not established. The main uncertainty is the missing workspace detail, which keeps this below medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external REST-backed resource, conflicts become possible.
IF a shared filesystem is added, concurrent edits could collide.
mitigations: Assign separate resources per agent.
Serialize any shared writes manually.
Use per-agent API tokens.
Check for duplicate updates after each run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which agent_b could plausibly consume as evaluation or downstream input. Because agent_b is an observability/evaluation tool with REST API access, a bad assumption from agent_a could propagate unless explicitly verified. This is inferred, not directly documented, so choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a-generated decisions are reused without review, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on agent_a outputs.
Add a verification step in agent_b.
Tag agent_a outputs as untrusted by default.
Compare outputs against source documents.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b has broad egress and no residency or retention controls are documented. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data flows from agent_a into agent_b. Only agent_a is directly cited for data class exposure because agent_b lacks such fields, which is itself part of the uncertainty.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from agent_a is sent to agent_b, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or residency requirements apply, the pair may violate them without extra controls.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer.
Block regulated data from agent_b.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Confirm residency requirements for any hosted endpoint.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
